messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It is a young, forming gas‑giant orbiting the star HD 100546, located about 350 light‑years away in the constellation Musca.  Its radius is roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter**, making it one of the biggest exoplanets ever detected.  

Other very large exoplanets include:

| Planet | Approximate radius (Jupiter radii) |
|--------|------------------------------------|
| HD 209458 b | ~1.3 |
| WASP‑17b | ~1.9 |
| HAT‑P‑32b | ~1.8 |

These values are based on transit and radial‑velocity measurements, and the exact size can vary slightly depending on the method used.  As of now, no planet larger than HD 100546 b has been confirmed.
